doc.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Bechet records and his early heroes
summary: He names his first 78 as a Sidney Bechet record, says he never heard Bechet live, and names Red Allen and J.C. Higginbotham as heroes.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: Could you tell me what that album was? No?
It was a 78. It was something called “Coal Black Shine” and “I Ain’t Gonna Give
Nobody None Of My Jelly Roll.”
Did you get a chance to hear Sidney Bechet perform?
Not in person, no. Never. I think I heard him on some of the Eddie Condon broadcasts, but I never saw him in person.
Yeah, cause he was an ex-pat, in Paris for many, many years.
So it’s a rarity to hear him actually in performance back here in the states there.
No I never did. I heard Bob Wilbur who was his disciple. He was pretty good, but... in fact I think he’s still going.
And my other hero was Henry “Red” Allen and J.C. Higginbotham.
